subject.title: fix(security): ignore string-literal contents in code-safety env/exfil rules (#82469)

question: After the nested-interpolation string masking gap is fixed, should OpenClaw accept env-harvesting-only string-literal masking as the code-safety scanner boundary?
rationale: The change reduces critical false positives but changes a security audit heuristic's view of source code, so tests alone should not settle the scanner boundary.

options.title: Fix then accept env-harvesting-only masking
options.body: Repair nested interpolation string masking, keep potential-exfiltration and payload rules unmasked, and merge after focused scanner validation plus security-owner review.

options.title: Require parser-backed scanning
options.body: Pause this heuristic implementation and require a syntax-aware tokenizer or parser before changing security-audit tokenization.

options.title: Accept the residual false-positive edge
options.body: A security owner may intentionally accept the remaining nested-interpolation false-positive class if the narrower improvement is worth landing immediately.

recommendation.title: Fix then accept env-harvesting-only masking
recommendation.body: Repair nested interpolation string masking, keep potential-exfiltration and payload rules unmasked, and merge after focused scanner validation plus security-owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: He is both a listed Security owner in CONTRIBUTING.md and the strongest recent current-main history signal on this scanner surface.
